newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TENNIS-BJORKMAN MOVES INTO TOP 50 WITH NZ WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BJORKMAN MOVES INTO TOP 50 WITH NZ WIN.

text.p: Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman moved from 65th in the world into the top 50 with a straight sets 7-6 (7-0) 6-0 win over Denmark's Kenneth Carlsen in the final of New Zealand's BellSouth Open tennis championship on Monday.
Bjorkman won $US43,000 ($NZ61,000) for taking the title while Carlsen collected $US25,300 as he lost his third finals appearance.
A delighted Bjorkman said the fourth game of the second set, where he forced five break points on Carlsen's service before finally prevailing, had been the crucial point in the match.
"The fourth game was very important. It was where it all happened, especially after Kenneth started off so well and was all over me early in the first set," he said.
"I struggled a bit in the first set but I made it to the tiebreak, and played a good tiebreak, then felt very strong after that."
Carlsen had raced to a 4-1 lead in the first set with two breaks of service before Bjorkman rallied to reel off three games in a row to level at 4-4.
He then whitewashed his opponent with a confident performance in the tiebreak and always looked in control of the second set.
The pair now fly to Melbourne to prepare for first-round matches at the Australian Open on Tuesday. Should they win, they will meet again in the second round, this time over five sets.
